Hi Maya — thanks for the note and for sending the redlines.

Short answers up front:
- BYOK persistence: Redwood does not persist customer-managed private keys on inference hosts in plaintext. We support both customer-managed KMS (BYOK) and Redwood-managed keys; when BYOK is used, private key material lives in the customer's KMS/HSM and we reference it via transient wrapped tokens.
- Emergency rotation: we have a documented emergency rotation playbook (internal) that includes immediate routing to a warm fallback key, audit logging, and a rollback window. We can provide a redacted runbook for review.
- Access controls: happy to share an access matrix for key ops.

We can do DocuSign — that works for our legal team. I'll loop in Grace (Security) and Marcus (Legal) to get concrete language for the TOMs exhibit and to confirm the DPA signature flow.

I can also do a 30-min call Thursday 6/24 11:00–11:30 PT if that works for you.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Head of Sales, Enterprise Accounts
Redwood Inference
[Sent from Redwood Console]

From: grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com

Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 08:50:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA redlines + TOMs clarifications

Tessa / Maya — thanks for the context. I dug into the redlines and sketched a short TOMs attachment that addresses the three asks. Key points:

- Key storage model: BYOK = private key material remains in customer KMS/HSM. Redwood only stores short-lived wrapped key handles and KV cache tokens; we never store unwrapped private key bytes on inference nodes.

- Approved KMS list (examples): AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS, Azure Key Vault, Thales Luna HSM (on-prem HSM integrations available with Private deployment). We will include language that new KMS vendors require notice + compatibility testing.

- Emergency rotation: proposed process — 1) notify account contacts + post incident ticket; 2) push clients to fallback key handle; 3) rotate handles in a planned window with audit events; 4) optional escrow-release if customer requests. We'll add SLA windows for acknowledgment and initial mitigation.

- Access matrix (summary):
  - Key Ops (grad-level group): rotate, view metadata, cannot extract private key material
  - Security (sec-admins): view audit trails, revoke handles
  - DevOps: deploy wrapped handles to runtime, no key material access

I'll attach the TOMs exhibit (toms_exhibit_v3.pdf) with inline comments for Marcus to check legal phrasing. Marcus, main ask from your side: carveouts or limitations we should add for cross-border export controls and subprocessor notification timing.

—Grace
Grace O'Connor
Director, Security Engineering
Redwood Inference
